doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Costumes, the clown outfit and the doubling variety troupe
summary: He wore a clown costume modelled on the Six Brown Brothers and sang romantic songs; everyone doubled in the variety show band.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Uh-huh. I had a clown costume to start off with. Uh-huh. Because I, uh, I was the kind of imitating, I got the idea from the Six Brown Brothers. You remember the old Six Brown Brothers? Yeah. Used to wear clown costumes, playing saxophone. They had a saxophone sextet they did. Yeah. Uh, that was one of my uniforms. That was starting. Then I used to sing romantic songs, you know. I had a fair voice too. You mean straight or?

Straight. Let me call you Sweetheart and Mahajie, man. I'd take off good on those numbers. Yeah? What did the other guys, what kind of a guy did you have? We had comedians, we, well it was a variety show. And how many musicians in there? Uh, that, uh, about four or five, all of you, we never had no straight comedians. Uh-huh. Everybody was doubling. Everybody had a doubling. Musicians had a double. What instruments? Them cats had to do everything.
This show had, uh, when I joined Dr. Moon, they had a violin player, had a banjo player, had a clarinet player, and they had a guitar player.
Uh-huh. That was a combination. Uh-huh. And two of them was comedians in this bunch. I see.
